confidence_notes: I ran three web searches. One returned the RBA rate. Two covered Leh food and drink prices. The food and drink results were mostly undated travel-blog and budget-site figures, not a cost-of-living index. They suggested a local meal of about Rs 150-300, a café meal of Rs 400-800, a restaurant beer of about Rs 150 (probably dated, so I raised it for current prices), and coffee of about Rs 150-200. I found no direct cappuccino or beer price for Leh. Cocktail and wine are estimated from the beer price: cocktail at about 1.7x beer, and wine by the glass at about 1.4x beer. Both are rarely listed in Leh and sometimes unavailable on dry days. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge, not from live listings. They assume July peak season, with high seasonal variability and few registered hostels. The USD/INR conversion for the food and drink estimates is approximate.
comparable_city_reasoning: Compared with other Indian Himalayan tourist towns such as Manali and McLeod Ganj. Leh is priced a little higher because of remote logistics and a short peak season, and a July pricing window is peak.
